title: `setParam()` Pattern

notebook.text:
The implementation provided is incorrect primarily because it fails to delegate unrecognized parameters to the superclass, which will prevent the behavior from handling standard IvP properties like priority, condition, and duration.
1
2
Corrected Code
bool BHV_Survey::setParam(string param, string val)
{
  if(param == "survey_radius") {
    double dval = atof(val.c_str());
    // Robustness: ensure value is a valid non-negative number [3]
    if((dval < 0) || (!isNumber(val)))
      return(false);
      
    m_radius = dval;
    return(true);
  }

  // CRITICAL: Delegate to superclass if not handled locally [1]
  return IvPBehavior::setParam(param, val);
}

MOOS-IvP-Specific Explanations
Superclass Delegation: Every IvP behavior inherits from the IvPBehavior superclass, which manages a large set of general configuration parameters (e.g., name, pwt, condition, endflag, updates, duration).
3
4
 If your subclass setParam() function returns false for these parameters without calling IvPBehavior::setParam(param, val), the helm will treat those critical mission-planning parameters as unrecognized.
1
 This typically results in a MALCONFIG state, preventing the mission from launching.
5
6
Semantic and Syntax Checking: Solid checking in setParam() reduces debugging headaches later.
7
 Using the isNumber() utility (part of the IvP utility library) is recommended because atof() returns zero when passed a non-numerical string, making it impossible to distinguish between a user intentionally setting a zero value and a syntax error in the .bhv file.
7
Dynamic Updates: This function is not only called during helm startup but also by the checkUpdates() function to apply dynamic parameter changes received via MOOS mail at runtime.
2
8
 If setParam() is incorrectly implemented, dynamic updates to your custom parameters (or the inherited ones) will be ignored, often resulting in a BHV_WARNING being posted to the MOOSDB.
8
9
Diagnostic Checklist for Behavior Parameters
Check the Helm State: If the helm comes up in MALCONFIG, inspect the terminal or appcasting output for "Configuration Warnings" identifying unrecognized parameters.
5
Verify Parameter Persistence: Use uHelmScope to see if your behavior is "Active" or "Running."
10
11
 If it stays "Idle," check if the condition parameter was correctly processed by the superclass.
12
Monitor Warnings: Scope on the MOOS variable BHV_WARNING at runtime.
9
 If your setParam() returns false during a dynamic update, the helm will post a "Faulty update" warning there.
8
